title: Original Sin
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Original sin means that humanity’s sin problem reaches the root of human nature through Adam’s fall. People do not merely become sinners by isolated actions; they are born into a fallen condition and need redemption in Christ.
summary: Original sin means that humanity’s sin problem reaches the root of human nature through Adam’s fall. People do not merely become sinners by isolated actions; they are born into a fallen condition and need redemption in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the last Adam who brings righteousness and life where Adam brought sin and death. Through Christ, fallen people receive grace, justification, new life, and the hope of restoration.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Original sin explains why the human problem is deeper than bad habits, poor choices, painful environments, or lack of education. Humanity’s fall in Adam brought sin, guilt, corruption, death, and separation from God into the human race.

People sin personally and willingly, but Scripture also teaches that sin is already at work in the human heart. Sinners are not morally neutral until they make enough bad choices. They are born into a fallen condition and need grace from the beginning.

This doctrine does not remove personal responsibility. Every person sins in real thoughts, desires, words, actions, and failures to do good. But original sin shows that personal sins flow from a deeper root.

The hope of Scripture is that Christ is greater than Adam’s ruin. Through Adam came sin and death, but through Christ comes righteousness and life. The Gospel answers the depth of the fall with a Savior strong enough to redeem fallen people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Original sin explains why the human problem runs deeper than behavior management, self-help, recovery progress, religious effort, or moral improvement. People do not merely need better habits; they need rescue from a fallen condition.

This doctrine also keeps people from pretending they can save themselves. The problem is too deep for willpower, religion, or self-reform. But the hope is greater than the ruin: where Adam brought sin and death, Christ brings righteousness and life to all who belong to Him.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Stop treating sin as something you can manage apart from grace. Confess your need honestly before God, reject pride and self-rescue, and look to Christ as the new Head who gives new life. Walk humbly, knowing your hope is not in being better than others, but in being made alive in Jesus.
